evidence.text:
Give every tree Entire writes to a single os.Root anchor

Entire does filesystem I/O in six trees, and until now each read and write
assembled its own absolute path and handed it to os.ReadFile/os.WriteFile.
Containment was therefore a property each call site had to keep honouring
by hand, and several of them carried comments saying so outright:
PluginDataDir "guarantees ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR always points inside the
managed data subtree", investigate.RunDir noted that "an unvalidated id
would be a path-traversal sink" feeding os.RemoveAll.

Each tree now has one package that owns a shared *os.Root over it, and the
names that reach those roots are relative to them:

  .entire                    entiredir
  git common dir             gitdir
  the working tree           worktreedir
  an agent's session store   agent.SessionStore
  per-user config / cache    userdirs.ConfigRoot / CacheRoot
  managed plugin tree        pluginRoot

The roots memoize through one registry, osroot.Shared, replacing three
separate copies of that map. Directory creation goes through
osroot.MkdirAllNoSymlink, which refuses a component that already exists as
a symlink -- os.Root blocks a symlink that escapes a root but follows one
pointing elsewhere inside it, and an escaping one otherwise surfaces as an
opaque errno far from the cause. entire doctor reports the symlinks that
are already there.

Two anchors are worth calling out because they close a real gap rather
than formalising an existing one. agen

# Review of `improve-context-management` Branch -- CLI Commands and Lifecycle Files

**Branch:** `improve-context-management`
**Base:** `main` (00c8469a)

Pin every path component instead of checking it and looking again

NoSymlinkedParent walked a name's parents with Lstat and then handed the
WHOLE name back to the original root, so the thing that was checked and
the thing that was opened were resolved twice, independently. Everything
in this package now opens each component in turn, keeps the descriptor,
and operates relative to it: OpenDirNoSymlinks descends one component at
a time, OpenParentNoSymlinks pins the parent and returns the leaf, and
ReadFileNoFollow, OpenFileNoFollow, LstatNoSymlinks, RemoveNoSymlinks,
ReadDirNoSymlinks and WalkDirNoSymlinks are all expressed on top of that
pair. NoSymlinkedParent survives as a predicate and now says in its own
doc that a caller acting on the result must re-open through
OpenParentNoSymlinks rather than trust it.

MkdirAllNoSymlink follows the same rule for the directories it creates,
so a component that appears between the check and the Mkdir is opened
and identity-checked like any other rather than being MkdirAll'd blind.
OpenChild stops reporting a regular file as ErrSymlinkedPath and returns
ErrWalkRootNotDirectory: replacing a link and replacing a file are
different remedies.

The atomic writers no longer fsync. The rename is what gives every
caller here the property it actually needs, that a reader never sees a
torn file; fsync buys durability across a power loss, and nothing
written through these functions is worth that — settings, session state,
